doc: Logfire's dialect. The request side has several overlapping spellings: `events`, `prompt`, and `all_messages_events` are primary, while `request_data` is read only when none of them supplied a conversation. `response_data` is always read because a request carrier must not suppress the answer. The paired generic Logfire capture exercises every branch, repeated history, and overlapping response evidence.

carriers.doc: The request as Logfire recorded it: a conversation the span received, which may re-state earlier turns.
The response payload, an array that expands into one observation per message.

The request conversation as an array of messages. It can include earlier assistant turns as context, so the carrier stays direction-neutral: classifying every member as input would hide that history from the span view.

A completed conversation assembled from the span's request and response. Because one array mixes both directions, assigning either direction to the carrier would misclassify some of its messages; roles and duplicate evidence distinguish the individual turns.

detect.doc: An instrumentation library identifying itself through telemetry.sdk.name - previously a Rust matcher, now one declared dimension.
detect.label: Logfire

messages.doc: Every carrier this dialect writes a conversation to, with the local order between them. The order is asymmetric: `request_data` is a fallback behind the three primary request spellings, while the answer side is unconditional. The paired generic capture proves that a duplicated request is not displayed twice, repeated prompt history collapses across spans, and a response repeated beside `all_messages_events` remains one answer.

branch_set.doc: Primary: the three request spellings. Fallback: the request payload, only if none of them supplied anything. Always: the response.

primary.doc: An events array carried as one attribute. Read in two passes, and the passes are the point: every recognised event is emitted before any grouped block, which is the order the code being replaced produced. A single interleaved scan would return the same messages in a different conversation.

passes.doc: Recognised message events, each tagged with its own name - downstream keys role derivation and ordering on that name, so tagging them alike would erase what the payload carries.

Everything else that carries structured data: this dialect emits multimodal content blocks as unnamed events, with the real content in `data` and a human-readable summary beside it. Runs of consecutive blocks of the same side become one message, because that is what they are - one turn's content, not one message per block. An event with no name reaches this pass, which is why the first condition is stated as 'not one of' rather than 'named something else'.

by.doc: Input blocks are the user's side.

primary.doc: The request as an array of messages.

alternatives.doc: The payload is an array of messages; non-objects are not turns.
The payload is an array of messages; non-objects are not turns.

fallback_if_primary_empty.doc: The request payload, read only when nothing else carried the conversation. It duplicates the input side that `events` also carries, which is why it is a fallback rather than another primary. Requires a non-empty `messages` array, so an empty request is not mistaken for one.

alternatives.doc: Kept whole; the structural reading happens at query time.

always.doc: The response. Read whatever the events said, and that asymmetry with the request below is deliberate: the answer is what was being dropped when one gate covered both. Two documented shapes - a structured message, or streamed text combined into one string.

alternatives.doc: Kept whole; the structural reading happens at query time.

messages.doc: Tools inside the request payload. Some Logfire integrations do not also set the convention's own carrier, which is exactly the condition - stated here, rather than as a global "nothing else produced tools" flag that any unrelated dialect could satisfy first. The generic Logfire capture exercises this path without a convention-side duplicate.

message_projections.doc: Instrumentation 6.x emits a successful input-only lifetime span beside the completed streaming-response log. It is retained as raw telemetry but omitted from the SideML conversation so one request is not shown as a second incomplete turn. Errors remain visible because they may have no completed companion.
